sections.sectionSummaryBrief: True joy comes from humility and self-nullification, where one recognizes their virtues as gifts from above, leading to complete joy.

translations.translation: And the explanation of the matter of joy that is in the aspect of self-nullification
(to the extent that even when the joy is in a state of revelation, it is nevertheless in the aspect of self-nullification),
behold, the true essence of joy comes from the side of humility and self-nullification,
as it is written,
"The humble will increase their joy in the L-rd."
And the explanation of the connection between humility and joy
(even though superficially they are two opposite matters),
is explained by the Alter Rebbe in the discourse "The humble will increase their joy in the L-rd"
[and in several discourses of our Rebbes and leaders after that,
and also in the aforementioned discourse of the Baal HaYom HaHuledes (the one whose birthday it is)],
that the matter of humility is not that the humble person is mistaken about himself and does not know his virtues,
but rather,
that even though he knows his virtues,
to the extent that he knows all his virtues
[for every Jew,
even those whose conduct is entirely improper,
not only do they have mitzvos, but the mitzvos fill their entire being,
and in the language of our Sages,
"they are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate,"
and especially since "Your people are all righteous"
and "all Jews are presumed to be kosher"],
nevertheless, he does not thereby become a [significant] entity in his own eyes, and certainly not in a state of yeshus (selfhood),
because he knows the truth that the virtues he has are not his own power and the strength of his hand, but rather were given to him
(the powers for this)
from Above,
and if these powers had been given to another, he too would be on this level,
and from the perspective of his humility and self-nullification, he thinks,
that if these powers were with another, he would reveal them even more.
And this humility
[since he knows his virtues,
but he does not thereby become a [significant] entity]
behold, not only does it not lead to the opposite of joy,
but on the contrary,
his humility and self-nullification
(that he thinks he does not deserve anything)
bring him to great and complete joy.
For the completeness of joy is specifically in one who is nullified,
as is explained at length in the discourse.
And since joy comes about because of humility and self-nullification,
therefore even the joy itself
(even when it is in revelation)
is in the aspect of self-nullification.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The life of Sarah encompasses the sefiros, and the phrase "the lives of Sarah" indicates a level above division where even the revealed is in nullification.

translations.translation: And this is [the meaning of] "And the life of Sarah was... the years of the life of Sarah,"
"And the life of Sarah was" refers to that which she merited to attain supernal life.
And it specifies in this: one hundred years, twenty years, and seven years, which correspond to all the sefiros.
And as explained in the discourse,
that "one hundred years" is the aspect of Arich [Anpin], as the aspect of Atik shines within it,
therefore it is said
("one hundred")
years in the singular,
and it can be said that in our case it is above the aspect of "one."
And "twenty years" is the aspect of Chochmah and Binah,
and "seven years" is the aspect of the seven emotional attributes,
the seven days of construction.
And afterwards it adds "the years of the life of Sarah,"
"hers were the lives,"
that the lives were hers
(also)
in a felt [conscious] way,
that in [divine] service this is the matter of self-nullification within joy
(also)
as it is in revelation
(as above from the discourse of the Baal HaYom HaHuledes).
And this is also the reason that at the conclusion "the years of the life of Sarah" it does not specify the numbers one hundred, twenty, and seven,
because this [matter] that even the felt [revelation] is in self-nullification,
which is the unification of two opposite matters
(felt [revelation] and self-nullification),
is from an aspect that is above division.
And this is the superiority of "the years of the life of Sarah" over "the life of Sarah was one hundred years, etc.,"
for the matter of one hundred years, twenty years, and seven years,
although it is most elevated,
as is also understood from Rashi's commentary on the verse,
nevertheless, they are three distinct matters,
but not so "the years of the life of Sarah," for they are all equal,
above division.
And from this aspect
(which is above division),
even the felt [revelation] is in self-nullification,
"hers were the lives."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Through the service of making even revealed joy a state of nullification, one attains mastery over life itself, as joy breaks all boundaries.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that through the matter of "hers were the lives" in [divine] service,
that even the felt [revelation]
(joy that is in revelation)
is in self-nullification
(as per the interpretation of the Baal HaYom HaHuledes on "hers were the lives"),
through this, "hers were the lives" is also actualized in its simple sense,
that the lives are hers and she becomes the master of the lives.
For joy breaks all boundaries,
and therefore, through joy in revelation
(and in the aspect of self-nullification)
there is a strengthening of life-force
(above measure and limitation),
and in the manner of the known concept
regarding Yitzchak
[whose concept is laughter and joy,
as above],
that the gevuros (severities) of Yitzchak are the matter of a strengthening of vitality
(and a strengthening of blessings),
to the extent of life in ultimate perfection,
analogous to "and we shall live before Him" which will be in the future to come.
